questions.q: Which of the following is/are extra-constitutional and extralegal device(s) for securing cooperation and coordination between the States in India? [1995] 1️⃣ The National Development Council 2️⃣ The Governor's Conference 3️⃣ Inter-State Council 4️⃣ Zonal Councils
questions.e: According to the solution, the National Development Council, Governor's Conference, and Zonal Councils are extra-constitutional or statutory bodies. The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263.

questions.q: Which of the following are matters on which a constitutional amendment is possible only with the ratification of the legislature of not less than one-half of the states? [1995] 1️⃣ Election of the President 2️⃣ Representation of states in the Parliament 3️⃣ Lists in the 7th Schedule 4️⃣ Abolition of the Legislature Council in a State
questions.e: Amendments affecting the federal structure, such as the President's election, representation of states in Parliament, and the 7th Schedule lists, require state ratification. The abolition of a Legislative Council under Article 169 does not require such ratification.

questions.q: Article 156 of the Constitution of India provides that a Governor shall hold office for a term of five year from the date on which he enters upon his office. Which of the following can be deduced from this? [1995] 1️⃣ No Governor can be removed from office till completion of his term 2️⃣ No Governor can continue in office beyond five years
questions.e: Article 156 states the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President and may resign. A Governor also continues to hold office until a successor enters, even after the five-year term expires.

questions.q: Which of the following are matters on which a constitutional amendment is possible only with the ratification of the legislature of not less than one-half of the states? [1995] 1️⃣ Election of the President 2️⃣ Representation of states in Parliament 3️⃣ Any of the Lists in the 7th Schedule 4️⃣ Abolition of the Legislature Council of a State
questions.e: Ratification by half the states is required for changes to the federal provisions like the election of the President, state representation in Parliament, and the 7th Schedule. Article 169 allows Parliament to abolish a Legislative Council via a specific state resolution without federal ratification.

questions.q: What is not explicitly stated in the Constitution of India but followed as a convention? [1995]
o: (c) All sections of India are to be represented in...
(a) The Finance Minister is to be a Member of the...
(b) The Prime Minister has to resign if he loses t...
(d) If both the President and the Vice-President d...
questions.e: The resignation of the Prime Minister upon losing majority is a convention based on the principle of collective responsibility. It is an unwritten practice followed in the parliamentary system.

questions.q: Which one of the following was not proposed by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment in the area of Panchayati Raj? [1997]
o: (d) The elections will be held in six months time...
(b) The States will constitute their Finance Commi...
(c) The Panchayati Raj functionaries will be disqu...
(a) Thirty percent seats in all elected rural loca...
questions.e: The two-child norm for disqualification was not part of the 73rd Amendment, though some states like Haryana and Odisha have implemented such rules independently.

questions.q: Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Reservation of thirty-three percent of seats for women in Parliament and State Legislature does not require any Constitutional amendment: Reason (R): Political parties contesting elections can allocate thirty-three percent of seats they contest to women candidates without any Constitutional amendment. In the context of the above two statements which one of the following is correct? [1997]
o: (a) Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
(d) A is false but R is true
(b) Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
(c) A is true but R is false
questions.e: Reservation of seats for women in legislatures requires a constitutional amendment, making the assertion false. However, political parties are free to voluntarily allocate tickets to women candidates without any law.

questions.q: Which of the following are/is stated in the Constitution of India? [1997] 1️⃣ The President shall not be a member of either House of Parliament 2️⃣ The Parliament shall consist of the President and two Houses
questions.e: Article 59 states the President shall not be a member of either House, and Article 79 defines Parliament as the President and the two Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).

questions.q: In the following quotation, "WE THE PEOPLE OF INDIA, having solemnly resolved to constitute India into a Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic and to secure to all its citizens: JUSTICE, social, economic and political; LIBERTY of thought, expression, belief faith and worship; EQUALITY of status and of opportunity: and to promote among them all; FRATERNITY assuring the dignity of the individual and the unity and the integrity of the Nation. In our Constituent Assembly this 'X' do hereby adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution.", 'X' stands for: [1997]
questions.e: The Preamble records the date of adoption of the Constitution as the 26th day of November, 1949.

questions.q: Which one of the following schedules of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding anti-defection Act? [1998]
questions.e: The Tenth Schedule, known as the anti-defection law, was added by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1985.

questions.q: The Constitution of India recognises: [1999]
questions.e: Under Articles 29 and 30, the Constitution recognizes minorities based on religion and language, though it does not define the term "minority."

questions.q: Consider the following statements: An amendment to the Constitution of India can be initiated by the: [1999] 1️⃣ Lok Sabha 2️⃣ Rajya Sabha 3️⃣ State Legislature 4️⃣ President
questions.e: Article 368 provides that a constitutional amendment can be initiated by either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha). State legislatures cannot initiate amendments.

questions.q: Consider the following statements about the recent amendments to the elections law by the Representation of the People (Amendment) Act 1996: 1️⃣ Any conviction for the offence of insulting the Indian National flag or the Constitution of Indian shall entail disqualification for contesting elections to Parliament and State Legislatures for six year from the date of conviction 2️⃣ There is an increase in the security deposit which a candidate has to make to contest the election to the Lok Sabha 3️⃣ A candidate cannot now stand for election from more than one Parliament Constituency 4️⃣ No election will now be countermanded on the death of a contesting candidate
questions.e: The 1996 amendment increased security deposits and disqualified those insulting national symbols. However, a candidate is allowed to contest from up to two constituencies, not just one.

questions.q: The 73rd Constitution Amendment Act, 1992 refers to the: [2000]
o: (c) laying the foundation for strong and vibrant P...
(b) generation of employment for the able bodied a...
(a) generation of gainful employment for the unemp...
(d) guarantee of right to life, liberty and securi...
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment added Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to provide a constitutional framework for the Panchayati Raj system.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides that it shall be the endeavour of every state to provide adequate facility for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage of education? [2001]
questions.e: Article 350-A, inserted by the 7th Amendment Act of 1956, mandates that states provide mother-tongue instruction at the primary level for linguistic minorities.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution of India? [2001]
o: (c) It contains the provisions regarding the administration of tribal areas
(a) It lists the distribution of powers between the Union and the states
(d) It allocates seats in the Council of States
(b) It contains the languages listed in the Constitution
questions.e: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) to the States and Union Territories.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists: List-I (Amendments): A. 69th Amendment, B. 75th Amendment, C. 18th Amendment, D. 83rd Amendment. List-II (Topics): 1. Rent Tribunals, 2. No SC reservation in Arunachal Panchayats, 4. 10th Finance Commission, 5. Delhi NCT status.
questions.e: The 69th Amendment gave Delhi NCT status; the 75th established Rent Tribunals; the 83rd exempted Arunachal Pradesh from SC reservations in Panchayats.

questions.q: If a new state of the Indian Union is to be created, which one of the following schedules of the Constitution must be amended? [2001]
questions.e: The First Schedule contains the names of the States and Union Territories; therefore, it must be amended whenever a new state is created.

questions.q: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists: List-1 (Article): A. Article 54, B. Article 75, C. Article 155, D. Article 164. List-II (Content): 1. Election of President, 2. Appointment of PM, 3. Appointment of Governor, 4. Appointment of CM.
questions.e: Article 54 relates to the President's election, Art 75 to the PM's appointment, Art 155 to the Governor's appointment, and Art 164 to the Chief Minister's appointment.

questions.q: Which one of the following amendments to the Indian Constitution empowers the President to send back any matter for reconsideration by the Council of Ministers? [2002]
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment made the Council's advice binding, but the 44th Amendment allowed the President to return advice for reconsideration once.

questions.q: The 93rd Constitution Amendment deals with the: [2002]
o: (a) continuation of reservation for backward classes in government employment
(c) reservation of 30 percent posts for women in government recruitments
(b) free and compulsory education for all children between the age of 6 and 14 years
(d) allocation of more number of parliamentary seats for recently created States
questions.e: Note: The PDF mentions 93rd Amendment inrelates to education for 6-14 years. (Note: Historically this is usually associated with the 86th Amendment; however, the provided text solutions cite 93rd for this specific provision).

questions.q: Match List-I (Article of Indian Constitution) with List -II (Provisions) and select the correct answer using the codes given below the lists: List-I: A. Article 16 (2), B. Article 29 (2), C. Article 30 (1), D. Article 31 (1). List-II: 1. Property rights, 2. No discrimination in public employment, 3. Minority educational institutions, 4. No denial of admission to state-aided institutions.
questions.e: Article 16(2) prohibits discrimination in public employment; Art 29(2) protects against denial of admission to state-aided schools; Art 30(1) grants minorities the right to establish schools; Art 31(1) relates to property.

questions.q: The purpose of the inclusion of Directive Principles of the State Policy in the Indian Constitution is to establish: [2002]
questions.e: While Fundamental Rights establish political democracy, the Directive Principles (DPSP) aim to establish social and economic democracy.

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Directive Principles of the State Policy deals with the promotion of international peace and security? [2002]
questions.e: Article 51 of the Constitution, under Directive Principles, directs the state to promote international peace and security.

questions.q: The Ninth Schedule to the Indian Constitution was added by: [2003]
questions.e: The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act in 1951 to protect land reform laws from judicial review.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution did the President give his asset to the ordinance on electoral reforms when it was sent back to him by the Union Cabinet without making any changes (in the year 2002)? [2003]
questions.e: Article 123 of the Indian Constitution grants the President the power to promulgate ordinances during the recess of Parliament.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution did the President make a reference to the Supreme Court to seek the Court's opinion on the Constitutional validity of the Election Commission's decision on deferring the Gujarat Assembly Elections (in the year 2002)? [2003]
questions.e: Article 143 provides for the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, where the President can seek its opinion on matters of law or fact.

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides that 'It shall be the duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance'? [2003]
questions.e: Article 355 mandates the Union to protect states from external aggression and internal disturbances and ensure governance according to the Constitution.

questions.q: Match List-I (Item in the Indian Constitution) with List-II (Country from which it was derived): A. Directive Principles, B. Fundamental Rights, C. Concurrent List, D. Union with greater powers to the Union. Countries: 1. Australia, 2. Canada, 3. Ireland, 5. United States.
questions.e: Directive Principles were derived from Ireland, Fundamental Rights from the US, Concurrent List from Australia, and the federal system with a strong center from Canada.

questions.q: Which of the following Constitutional Amendments are related to raising the number of Members of Lok Sabha to be elected from the States? [2003]
questions.e: The 7th Amendment (1956) and the 31st Amendment (1973) were instrumental in increasing the Lok Sabha's membership from the states.

questions.q: Which one of the following schedules of the Indian Constitution lists the names of states and specifies their territories? [2003]
questions.e: The First Schedule of the Constitution lists the names of all States and Union Territories and defines their territorial jurisdiction.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements correctly describes the Fourth Schedule of the Constitution of India? [2004]
o: (c) It contains the provisions regarding the administration of tribal areas
(d) It allocates seats in the Council of States
(b) It contains the languages listed in the Constitution
(a) It contains the scheme of the distribution of powers between the Union and the States
questions.e: The Fourth Schedule is dedicated to the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles of the Constitution of India says that the executive power of every State shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union? [2004]
questions.e: Article 257 stipulates that state executive power must be used so as not to hinder the Union's executive power.

questions.q: Match List I (Articles) with List II (Provision): A. Article 14, B. Article 15, C. Article 16, D. Article 17. Provisions: 1. Non-discrimination, 2. Equality before law, 3. Untouchability abolition, 4. Equality of opportunity in employment.
questions.e: Article 14 guarantees equality before law; Article 15 prohibits discrimination; Article 16 ensures equal employment opportunity; Article 17 abolishes untouchability.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India says, 'No child below the age of fourteen years shall the employed to work in any factory or mine or engaged in any other hazardous employment'? [2004]
questions.e: Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines, or hazardous jobs.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Part IX of the Constitution of India provisions for Panchyats and was inserted by the Constitution (Amendment) Act, 1992. 2️⃣ Part IX A of the Constitution of India contains provisions for Municipalities and the Article 243 Q envisages two types of Municipalities a Municipal Council and a Municipal Corporation for every State. [2005]
questions.e: Part IX (Panchayats) was added by the 73rd Amendment. Part IXA (Municipalities) was added by the 74th Amendment. Statement 2 is considered incorrect in the solution because Article 243Q actually envisages three types: Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Article 371 A to 371 I were inserted in the Constitution of India to meet regional demands of Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunchal Pradesh and Goa. 2️⃣ Constitution of India and the United States of America envisage a dual policy (The Union and the States) but a single cititzenship. 3️⃣ A naturalized citizen of India can never be deprived of his citizenship. [2005]
questions.e: Articles 371 A-I provide special provisions for several states. Statement 2 is false because the US has dual citizenship. Statement 3 is false because naturalized citizens can be deprived of citizenship if obtained by fraud.

questions.q: The Constitution (98th Amendment) Act is related to: [2005]
o: (c) readjustment of electoral constituencies on the basis of the population census 2001
(b) the Constitution of the National Judicial Commission
(d) the demarcation of new boundaries between States
(a) empowering the centre to levy and appropriate service tax
questions.e: The 98th Amendment Bill sought to create a National Judicial Commission for appointing and transferring judges.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Constitution of India has 20 parts. 2️⃣ There are 390 Articles in the Constitution of India in all. 3️⃣ Ninth, Tenth, Eleventh and Twelfth Schedules were added to the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Amendment) Acts. [2005]
questions.e: The original Constitution had 22 parts and 395 articles (now more). The 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th Schedules were indeed added later via various amendments.

questions.q: Who among the following was the chairman of the Union Constitution Committee of the Constituent Assembly? [2005]
questions.e: Jawaharlal Nehru chaired the Union Constitution Committee and the Union Power Committee.

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects is under the Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India? [2006]
o: (a) Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields
questions.e: Agriculture, Fisheries, and Public Health are State subjects. Regulation of labor and safety in mines and oilfields is a Union subject under Entry 55.

questions.q: What does the 104th Constitution Amendment Bill related to? [2006]
o: (d) Providing quota for religious minorities in th...
(a) Abolition of Legislative Councils in certain s...
(b) Introduction of dual citizenship for persons o...
(c) Providing quota to socially and educationally...
questions.e: The 104th Amendment Bill (which became the 93rd Amendment Act) provided for reservations in private aided and unaided educational institutions for backward classes.

questions.q: Which one among the following commission was set up in pursuance of a definite provision under an Article of the Constitution of India? [2006]
questions.e: The Election Commission is a constitutional body established under Article 324.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ Free and compulsory education to the children of 6-14 years age-group by the State by the seventy-sixth Amendment to the Constitution of India. 2️⃣ Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan seeks to provide computer education even in rural areas. 3️⃣ Education was included in the Concurrent List by the Forty-second Amendment, 1976 to the Constitution of India'. [2006]
questions.e: Statement 1 is false because education for 6-14 years was added by the 86th Amendment, not the 76th. Statement 3 is correct as education moved from the State to the Concurrent List in 1976.

questions.q: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Acts seeks that the size of the Councils of Ministers at the Centre and in a State must not exceed 15 per cent of the total number of members in the Lok Sabha and the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State, respectively? [2007]
questions.e: The 91st Constitutional Amendment Act of 2003 limited the size of the Council of Ministers to 15% of the total strength of the respective lower house.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are included in the Directive Principles of the State Policy? [2008] 1️⃣ Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour 2️⃣ Prohibition of consumption except for medicinal purposes of intoxicating drinks and of other drugs which are injurious to health
questions.e: Prohibition of traffic in human beings is a Fundamental Right (Article 23). Prohibition of intoxicating drinks is a Directive Principle (Article 47).

questions.q: Which Schedule of the Constitution of India contains: Special provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas in several States? [2008]
questions.e: The Fifth Schedule deals with the administration of Scheduled Areas and Tribes in states other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram.

questions.q: Under which one of the following Constitution Amendment Acts, four languages were added to the list of languages under the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India, thereby raising their number to 22? [2008]
questions.e: The 92nd Amendment Act (2003) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule.

questions.q: Which one of the following Constitutional Amendments states that the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Minister shall not exceed fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of the People? [2009]
questions.e: The 91st Amendment (2003) restricted the size of the Council of Ministers at the Centre and in the States to 15%.

questions.q: With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following: 1️⃣ Fundamental Rights 2️⃣ Fundamental Duties 3️⃣ Directive Principles of the State Policy [2010] Which of the above provisions of the Constitution of India is/are fulfilled by the National Social Assistance Programme launched by the government of India?
questions.e: The National Social Assistance Programme fulfills Article 41 of the Directive Principles, which relates to the right to public assistance in certain cases.

questions.q: Under the Constitution of India, which one of the following is not a fundamental duty? [2011-1]
o: (d) To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals
questions.e: Voting in public elections is a legal or political right, but it is not listed among the Fundamental Duties in Article 51A.

questions.q: Consider the following provisions under the Directive Principles of State Policy as enshrined in the Constitution of India: [2012-1] 1️⃣ Securing for citizens of India a uniform civil code 2️⃣ Organizing village Panchayats 3️⃣ Promoting cottage industries in rural areas 4️⃣ Securing for all the workers reasonable leisure and cultural opportunities Which of the above are the Gandhian Principles that are reflected in the Directive Principles of State Policy?
questions.e: Organizing village Panchayats (Article 40) and promoting cottage industries (Article 43) are specifically classified as Gandhian principles.

questions.q: Which of the following special powers have been conferred on the Rajya Sabha by the Constitution of India? [2012-1]
o: (d) To determine the functions of the Election Com...
(c) To amend the election procedure of the Preside...
(b) To pass a resolution empowering the Parliament...
(a) To change the existing territory of a State an...
questions.e: Under Articles 249 and 312, the Rajya Sabha has special powers to authorize Parliament to legislate on state subjects and create new All India Services.

questions.q: Which of the following provisions of the Constitution of India have a bearing on Education? [2012-1] 1️⃣ Directive Principles of State Policy 2️⃣ Rural and Urban Local Bodies 3️⃣ Fifth Schedule 4️⃣ Sixth Schedule 5️⃣ Seventh Schedule
questions.e: Provisions for education are found in the DPSP, the powers of local bodies, the administration of tribal areas (5th and 6th Schedules), and the division of powers (7th Schedule).

questions.q: According to the Constitution of India, it is the duty of the President of India to cause to be laid before the Parliament which of the following? [2012-1] 1️⃣ The Recommendations of the Union Finance Commission 2️⃣ The Report of the Public Accounts Committee 3️⃣ The Report of the Comptroller and Auditor General 4️⃣ The Report of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes
questions.e: The President causes reports from the Finance Commission, CAG, and SC/ST Commissions to be laid. The Public Accounts Committee report is submitted by the committee itself to Parliament.

questions.q: Which of the following is/are among the Fundamental Duties of citizens laid down in the Indian Constitution? [2012-1] 1️⃣ To preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture 2️⃣ To protect the weaker sections from social injustice 3️⃣ To develop the scientific temper and spirit of inquiry 4️⃣ To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity
questions.e: Preserving heritage, developing scientific temper, and striving for excellence are Fundamental Duties. Protecting weaker sections is a Directive Principle, not a duty.

questions.q: The distribution of powers between the Centre and the States in the Indian Constitution is based on the Act provided in the [2012-1]
questions.e: The current federal distribution of powers in India is largely inherited from the framework established by the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.q: With reference to Indian History, the Members of the Constituent Assembly from the Provinces were [2013-1]
o: (a) directly elected by the people of those Provinces
(d) selected by the Government for their expertise in constitutional matters
(b) nominated by the Indian National Congress and the Muslim League
(c) elected by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies
questions.e: Members of the Constituent Assembly were indirectly elected by the members of the Provincial Legislative Assemblies.

questions.q: According to the Constitution of India, which of the following are fundamental for the governance of the country? [2013-1]
questions.e: Article 37 specifically states that the Directive Principles are fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the state to apply them in making laws.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2013-1] 1️⃣ An amendment to the Constitution of India can be initiated by an introduction of a bill in the Lok Sabha only. 2️⃣ If such an amendment seeks to make changes in the federal character of the Constitution, the amendment also requires to be ratified by the legislature of all the States of India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Amendments can be initiated in either House of Parliament. Federal changes require ratification by at least half of the states, not all states.

questions.q: Which of the following bodies does not/do not find mention in the Constitution? [2013-1] 1️⃣ National Development Council 2️⃣ Planning Commission 3️⃣ Zonal Councils
questions.e: All three are non-constitutional bodies. The NDC and Planning Commission were created by resolutions, while Zonal Councils were created by an Act of Parliament.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2013-1] 1️⃣ National Development Council is an organ of the Planning Commission. 2️⃣ The Economic and Social Planning is kept in the Concurrent List in the Constitution of India. 3️⃣ The Constitution of India prescribes that Panchayats should be assigned the task of preparation of plans for economic development and social justice. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: NDC is separate from the Planning Commission. Economic planning is in the Concurrent List (Entry 20), and Article 40/73rd Amendment empowers Panchayats for economic planning.

questions.q: 'Economic Justice' as one of the objectives of the Indian Constitution has been provided in [2013-1]
o: (a) the Preamble and the Fundamental Rights
(c) the Fundamental Rights and the Directive Principles of State Policy
(b) the Preamble and the Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: The Preamble promises "Justice-social, economic and political," and the DPSP (like Article 38) aims to promote welfare by securing a social order with economic justice.

questions.q: Which one of the following Schedules of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding anti-defection? [2014-1]
questions.e: The Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) was added to prevent political defections.

questions.q: In the Constitution of India, promotion of international peace and security is included in the [2014-1]
questions.e: Promotion of international peace and security is a Directive Principle under Article 51.

questions.q: The provisions in Fifth Schedule and Sixth Schedule in the Constitution of India are made in order to [2015-1]
o: (c) determine the powers, authority and responsibilities of Panchayats
(a) protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes
(d) protect the interests of all the border States
questions.e: The Fifth and Sixth Schedules provide for the administration and protection of the interests of Scheduled Tribes and Tribal Areas.

questions.q: Who/Which of the following is the custodian of the Constitution of India? [2015-1]
questions.e: The Supreme Court of India acts as the apex court and the final custodian and interpreter of the Constitution.

questions.q: "To uphold and protect the Sovereignty, Unity and Integrity of India" is a provision made in the [2015-1]
questions.e: Protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India is one of the Fundamental Duties listed in Article 51A.

questions.q: The ideal of 'Welfare State' in the Indian Constitution is enshrined in its [2015-1]
questions.e: The Directive Principles (DPSP) are specifically intended to establish a welfare state by providing socio-economic guidelines.

questions.q: Consider the following statements regarding the Directive Principles of State Policy: [2015-1] 1️⃣ The Principles spell out the socio-economic democracy in the country. 2️⃣ The provisions contained in these Principles are not enforceable by any court. Which of the statements given above is / are correct?
questions.e: DPSPs aim for socio-economic democracy and are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts), unlike Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: The Parliament of India acquires the power to legislate on any item in the State List in the national interest if a resolution to that effect is passed by the [2016-1]
o: (d) Rajya Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its members present and voting
(b) Lok Sabha by a majority of not less than two-thirds of its total membership
(c) Rajya Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
(a) Lok Sabha by a simple majority of its total membership
questions.e: Under Article 249, the Rajya Sabha can empower Parliament to legislate on a State subject by passing a resolution with a 2/3rd majority of members present and voting.

questions.q: Which one of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India? [2017-1]
questions.e: The Preamble promises Liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith, and worship. It mentions Economic Justice, but not economic liberty.

questions.q: The mind of the makers of the Constitution of India is reflected in which of the following? [2017-1]
o: (c) The Directive Principles of State Policy
questions.e: As noted by Constituent Assembly members, the Preamble embodies the dreams and vision of the makers of the Constitution.

questions.q: Which of the following are envisaged by the Right against Exploitation in the Constitution of India? [2017-1] 1️⃣ Prohibition of traffic in human beings and forced labour 2️⃣ Abolition of untouchability 3️⃣ Protection of the interests of minorities 4️⃣ Prohibition of employment of children in factories and mines
questions.e: The Right against Exploitation specifically covers Articles 23 (trafficking/forced labor) and 24 (child labor). Abolition of untouchability is part of the Right to Equality.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct? [2017-1]
o: (d) Rights are privileges of a few citizens against the many.
(a) Rights are claims of the State against the citizens.
(b) Rights are privileges which are incorporated in the Constitution of a State.
(c) Rights are claims of the citizens against the State.
questions.e: Rights represent the demands and claims of individual citizens that they make upon the state.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are true of the Fundamental Duties of an Indian citizen? [2017-1] 1️⃣ A legislative process has been provided to enforce these duties. 2️⃣ They are correlative to legal duties.
questions.e: Many duties are enforced via specific laws (like the Environment Protection Act). They are correlative as citizens must abide by laws that often mirror these duties.

questions.q: In the context of India, which one of the following is the correct relationship between Rights and Duties? [2017-1]
o: (c) Rights, not Duties, are important for the advancement of the personality of the citizen.
(d) Duties, not Rights, are important for the stability of the State.
(b) Rights are personal and hence independent of society and Duties.
questions.e: Rights and duties are two sides of the same coin; they are inseparable and correlative.

questions.q: Which principle among the 'following was added to the Directive Principles of State Policy by the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution? [2017-1]
o: (a) Equal pay for equal work for both men and women
(c) Right to work, education and public assistance
(b) Participation of workers in the management of industries
(d) Securing living wage and human conditions of work to workers
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment added Article 43A, which concerns the participation of workers in the management of industries.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: With reference to the Constitution of India, the Directive Principles of State Policy constitute limitations upon 1️⃣ legislative function, 2️⃣ executive function. [2017-1]
questions.e: Directive Principles are positive obligations or guidelines for the state; they do not act as legal limitations on legislative or executive powers like Fundamental Rights do.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The Parliament of India can place a particular law in the Ninth Schedule of the Constitution of Indi(a) 2️⃣ The validity of a law placed in the Ninth Schedule cannot be examined by any court and no judgement can be made on it. [2018-1]
questions.e: While Parliament can add laws to the Ninth Schedule, the Supreme Court ruled in the I.R. Coelho case (2007) that these laws are not immune to judicial review.

questions.q: In the federation established by The Government on India Act of 1935. Residuary Power were given to the [2018-1]
questions.e: Under the 1935 Act, the Governor General held the residuary powers, unlike the current Constitution where they belong to Parliament.

questions.q: Which one of the following reflects the nicest, appropriate relationship between law and liberty? [2018-1]
o: (a) If there are more laws, there is less liberty.
(b) If there are no laws, there is no liberty.
(d) If laws are changed too often, liberty is in danger.
(c) If there is liberty, laws have to be made by the people.
questions.e: As per liberal thought, the absence of law leads to anarchy where liberty cannot exist. Law provides the restraints necessary for everyone to enjoy liberty.

questions.q: Which of the following are regarded as the main features of the "Rule of Law"? 1️⃣ Limitation of powers 2️⃣ Equality before law 3️⃣ People's responsibility to the Government 4️⃣ Liberty and civil rights [2018-1]
questions.e: Rule of Law includes equality before the law, limitation of government powers, and protection of individual liberty. "Responsibility to the government" is not a standard feature.

questions.q: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement? [2018-1]
o: (d) Article 24 and the provisions under the 44th Amendment to the Constitution
(b) Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
(c) Article 21 and the freedoms guaranteed in Part. III
(a) Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution
questions.e: The Supreme Court (Puttaswamy case) declared the Right to Privacy as part of Article 21 and the liberties in Part III.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The 44th Amendment to the Constitution of India introduced an Article placing the election of the Prime Minister beyond judicial review. 2️⃣ The Supreme Court of India struck down the 99th Amendment to the Constitution of India as being violative of the independence of the judiciary. [2019-1]
questions.e: The 39th Amendment (not 44th) tried to place the PM's election beyond review. The SC did strike down the 99th Amendment (NJAC) to protect judicial independence.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: 1️⃣ The motion to impeach a judge of the supreme court of India cannot be rejected by the speaker of the Lok Sabha as per the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 2️⃣ The constitution of India defines and gives details of what constitutes 'incapacity and proved misbehaviour' of the judges of the Supreme Court of India. 3️⃣ The details of the process of the impeachment of the judges of the Supreme Court of India are given in the judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. 4️⃣ If the motion of the impeachment of a judge is taken up for voting, the law requires the motion to be backed by each house of the parliament and supported by a majority of total membership of that house and by not less than two-thirds of total members of that House present and voting. [2019-1]
questions.e: The Speaker can reject an impeachment motion. The Constitution does not define 'incapacity'. The process is in the 1968 Act and requires a special majority in Parliament.

questions.q: Under which schedule of the Constitution of India can the transfer of tribal land to private parties for mining be declared null and void? [2019-1]
questions.e: Under the Fifth Schedule, the Governor can regulate or prohibit the transfer of land to protect the interests of Scheduled Tribes.

questions.q: With reference to the constitution of India, prohibition or limitations or provisions contained in ordinary laws cannot act as prohibitions or limitations on the constitutional powers under Article 142. It could mean which one of the following? [2019-1]
o: (d) State Legislatures can not make laws on certai...
(c) In the event of grave financial crises in the...
(a) The decisions taken by the Election Commision...
(b) The Supreme Court of India is not constrained...
questions.e: Article 142 provides the Supreme Court with broad powers to do "complete justice," which are not restricted by ordinary parliamentary laws.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017? [2019-1] 1️⃣ Pregnant women are entitled for three months pre-delivery and three months post-delivery paid leave 2️⃣ Enterprises with creches must allow the mother minimum six creche visits daily 3️⃣ Women with two children get reduced entitlements.
questions.e: Mothers with 2+ children get 12 weeks of leave instead of 26. The Act requires 4 creche visits per day, not 6.

questions.q: With reference to the Constitution of India, consider the following statements: [2019-1] 1️⃣ No High Court shall have the jurisdiction to declare any central law to be constitutionally invalid. 2️⃣ An amendment to the Constitution of India cannot be called into question by the Supreme Court of India. Which of the statements given above is/ are correct?
questions.e: Both High Courts and the Supreme Court have the power of judicial review to strike down central laws or constitutional amendments if they violate the Constitution.

questions.q: A parliamentary system of government is one in which [2020-1]
o: (b) The government is responsible to the parliamen...
(d) The government is elected by the people and ca...
(a) All political parties in the parliament are re...
(c) The government is chosen by the parliament but...
questions.e: In a parliamentary system, the executive is collectively responsible to the legislature (specifically the Lok Sabha), which can remove it via a no-confidence vote.

questions.q: Which part of the Constitution of India declares the ideal of Welfare state? [2020-1]
questions.e: Part IV (Directive Principles) aims to establish a social and economic order that promotes the welfare of the people.

questions.q: Consider the following statements: [2020-1] 1️⃣ The Constitution of India defines its 'basic structure in terms of federalism, secularism, fundamental rights and democracy. 2️⃣ The Constitution of India provides for 'judicial review' to safeguard the citizens' liberties and to preserve the ideals on which the constitution is based. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Constitution does not define 'basic structure'; it is a judicial invention. Judicial review is provided (e.g., Article 13) to protect rights and constitutional ideals.

questions.q: One common agreement between Gandhism and Marxism is [2020-1]
o: (a) The final goal of a stateless society
questions.e: Both Gandhi (as a philosophical anarchist) and Marx (predicting the 'withering away of the state') aimed for a stateless society.

questions.q: The Preamble to the Constitution of India is [2020-1]
o: (a) A part of the Constitution but has no legal effect
(b) Not a part of the Constitution and has no legal effect either
(c) A part of the Constitution and has the same legal effect as any other part
(d) A part of the Constitution but has no legal effect independently of other parts
questions.e: The Supreme Court (Keshavananda case) ruled the Preamble is a part of the Constitution, but it is not enforceable in court independently.

questions.q: With reference to the provisions contained in part IV of the constitution of India, which of the following statements is/ are correct? [2020-1] 1️⃣ They shall be enforceable by courts 2️⃣ They shall not be enforceable by any court 3️⃣ The principles laid down in this part are to influence the making of laws by the state
questions.e: Article 37 states that Directive Principles are non-enforceable by courts but are fundamental in the governance of the country and should be applied in law-making.

questions.q: Other than the Fundamental Rights, which of the following parts of the Constitution of India reflect/reflects the principles and provisions of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)? [2020-1] 1️⃣ Preamble 2️⃣ Directive Principles of State Policy 3️⃣ Fundamental Duties
questions.e: The Preamble (dignity), DPSP (right to work/welfare), and Fundamental Duties (individual obligations) all mirror concepts found in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
